gap: No result ChatGPT got gives the electricity cost per pint removed for each built-in-pump model. AlorAir's own L/kWh figures show that the Sentinel HD35P WiFi Dealectric lists (2.0 L/kWh) costs about $4.30 in power per 100 pints removed. The HD35PS WiFi (2.47 L/kWh), with the same 35 AHAM pints, the same 15.2×11.2×11.4 in body and the same 19.6 ft pump lift, costs about $3.48. The Galaxy 85P (2.7 L/kWh) is the cheapest to run at about $3.18 and also has the lowest price per AHAM pint/day at $8.46.
standout_why: Rivals checked: crawlspacedehumidifiers.org/with-pump (cited) gives an energy factor only for the HDi90 (2.69 L/kWh) and Seaira NXT85C, with no electricity rate and no running cost. dehumidifierverdict.com (cited) gives only an approximate price per AHAM pint, with no wattage or L/kWh. Neither has a cost per pint removed, a yearly running cost, or the HD35P vs HD35PS efficiency gap. crawlclimate.com (cited) would not load (self-signed certificate error), so it was not checked. The finding is new and useful. It only changes which variant we list in the small slot, and every efficiency input is a maker claim with no named test condition, so I scored it 2 rather than 3.
decides: Small slot: replace the Sentinel HD35P WiFi (2.0 L/kWh, $438.92) with the Sentinel HD35PS WiFi (2.47 L/kWh, $454.48). At 12 h/day it uses about 287 kWh (~$52) less per year, which covers the $15.56 price gap in about 4 months. Large slot: keep the Galaxy 85P, which has the lowest $/AHAM pint ($8.46) and the lowest cost per 100 pints ($3.18), but say its stated operating floor is 37.4°F against 33.8°F for the Sentinels. Mid slot: the HDi65S (2.4 L/kWh, $566.75) is slightly cheaper to buy and run than the HD55P (2.3 L/kWh, $583.28), but the HD55P figure is uncertain (see the HD55P note).
